name: Catchment hydrology
shortDescription: Land uses alter water quantity and quality delivered to the stream.
definition: Represents watershed-scale drivers that change runoff, infiltration, and pollutant delivery. It reflects how land cover and management shape the volume and timing of water entering the stream network.
functionStatement: Runoff and infiltration sustain natural flow regime, carry appropriate sediment and nutrients from uplands, and reliably cue spawning/migration of aquatic life.

name: Surface water storage
shortDescription: Natural or artificial storage attenuates flows and increases residence time.
definition: Represents the capacity of wetlands, ponds, and floodplain features to store water. Storage moderates peak flows and supports baseflow by slowing runoff.
functionStatement: Wetlands and storage features store floodwater, recharge groundwater, sustain baseflow, and provide low-velocity habitat.

name: Reach inflow
shortDescription: Local inputs alter magnitude, timing, and quality of flow.
definition: Captures tributaries, ditches, pipes, and other local inflows that change discharge or water quality at the reach scale.
functionStatement: Quantity + quality of inflow (tributaries, ditches, and pipes) does not provide harmful peaks or pollution, and supports diverse habitat conditions.

name: Streamflow regime
shortDescription: Characteristic flow pattern that shapes habitat and transport.
definition: Represents the timing, magnitude, frequency, and duration of flow events that structure physical and ecological processes.
functionStatement: Integrates the range of "typical" flows experienced by other processes. Examines the degree to which upstream infrastructure or land uses have fundamentally altered flow regimes (e.g., hydropeaking, dams, withdrawals).

name: Low flow and baseflow dynamics
shortDescription: Maintains wetted habitat and moderates conditions during low water.
definition: Represents how low flows sustain habitat, temperature moderation, and water quality during dry periods.
functionStatement: Ensures habitat availability and water quality during low water levels, and indicates non-storm conditions experienced the majority of the time.

name: High flow dynamics
shortDescription: Drives erosion and channel maintenance during peaks.
definition: Represents the energy of high flows that mobilize sediment, shape channels, and connect to floodplains.
functionStatement: Peak flows reshape channel without chronic instability, redistribute wood and sediment, reset habitats, and supply nutrients to floodplains.

name: Floodplain connectivity
shortDescription: Lateral exchange supports nutrient cycling and habitat.
definition: Represents how often and how effectively the channel connects with its floodplain to exchange water, sediment, and organic matter.
functionStatement: Frequent overbank flows reduce flood peaks, support riparian vegetation, create off-channel refugia, and extend nutrient processing time.

name: Hyporheic connectivity
shortDescription: Surface-subsurface exchange supports temperature and nutrient regulation.
definition: Represents exchange between surface water and shallow subsurface flow paths that influence temperature, nutrients, and habitat.
functionStatement: Surface water-groundwater exchange moderates temperature, transforms nutrients, supplies oxygen, and supports aquatic life.

name: Channel evolution
shortDescription: Changes in channel dimensions and slope reflecting adjustment.
definition: Represents the stage of channel adjustment driven by legacy impacts, altered flows, or sediment imbalance.
functionStatement: Long-term changes in channel size and slope maintain dynamic equilibrium and diverse habitats while interacting with the floodplain.

name: Channel and floodplain dynamics
shortDescription: Bank processes and planform dynamics that affect complexity.
definition: Represents lateral migration, bar formation, and floodplain building that create channel complexity.
functionStatement: Examines the role of bank processes and erosion in channel change. Observes patterns in sinuosity and curvature affecting habitat complexity.

name: Sediment continuity
shortDescription: Balanced sediment supply and transport maintaining form and habitat.
definition: Represents whether sediment supply, transport, and storage are in balance for the reach and watershed.
functionStatement: Balanced sediment supply and transport preserves bed elevations, substrate sizes, spawning/benthic habitats, and supports riparian succession.

name: Bed composition and bedform dynamics
shortDescription: Substrate and bedforms (and wood effects) supporting habitat and exchange.
definition: Represents the size, sorting, and structure of bed materials and bedforms that support habitat and hyporheic exchange.
functionStatement: Supports aquatic habitats through streambed material and bedform dynamics. Enhances habitat complexity and streambank stability.

name: Light and thermal regime
shortDescription: Regulates temperature and energy inputs shaping chemistry.
definition: Represents shading, solar input, and thermal buffering that influence water temperature and ecosystem metabolism.
functionStatement: Shade, solar input, and groundwater keep temperature and light within natural ranges for stream metabolism and dissolved oxygen.

name: Carbon processing
shortDescription: Organic matter dynamics supporting food webs and metabolism.
definition: Represents inputs, storage, and breakdown of organic matter that drive ecosystem respiration and production.
functionStatement: Organic matter is captured and broken down, fueling food webs, balancing production/ respiration, moderating pH/ redox, and supplying nutrients.

name: Nutrient cycling
shortDescription: N and P transformations controlling productivity and water quality.
definition: Represents uptake, retention, and transformation of nutrients within the stream corridor.
functionStatement: Nitrogen and phosphorus transformations feed primary production, regulate excess loads, and store or release nutrients.

name: Water and soil quality
shortDescription: Contaminants and constituents influencing chemical condition.
definition: Represents chemical stressors in water and soils that affect aquatic life and system health.
functionStatement: Physical and chemical processes limit pollutants, retain beneficial constituents, and protect ecological and human uses.

name: Habitat provision
shortDescription: Physical habitat diversity supporting life stages and taxa.
definition: Represents the variety and quality of physical habitats that support organisms across life stages.
functionStatement: Channel and floodplain structure supply depth, velocity, substrate diversity, and vegetation to support native organisms through all life stages.

name: Population support
shortDescription: Survival, reproduction, and movement of key taxa.
definition: Represents the capacity of the reach to sustain populations, including access to spawning and rearing areas.
functionStatement: Physical and chemical conditions enable spawning, juvenile growth, migration, and stress survival of target taxa.

name: Community dynamics
shortDescription: Balanced assemblages of native taxa and resilience.
definition: Represents community composition, diversity, and invasive pressure within the reach.
functionStatement: Species interactions sustain biodiversity, restrain invasives, and build resilience to disturbance.

name: Watershed connectivity
shortDescription: Longitudinal and lateral connectivity enabling recovery.
definition: Represents connectivity that enables recolonization, gene flow, and recovery after disturbance.
functionStatement: Continuous pathways for free movement of water, sediment, and organisms supporting recolonization, maintaining species diversity, and enabling recovery.
